utterances.text: They're benefiting from New York City taxpayers.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I would think when a contractor may have caused a failure involving 911, the contractor can't be the only one grading its own homework.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I guess my broader question, and this is particularly relevant a couple of days before the anniversary of September 11th, where so much was written about and discussed regarding the radios that the firefighters were using.

utterances.text: How dependent is the city on Motorola right now?

Gelobter says Motorola plays a big role across multiple services but the city should never be tied to one vendor for life. chapters.title: Morano questions city's dependence on Motorola and ability to replace them

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: If the city decided tomorrow that Motorola's performance was unacceptable, could we realistically replace them?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And how long would that take?

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: Thank you for that question.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: Motorola plays a big part, not just in emergency services, not just in the 911 managed service, not just in next generation 911.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: They also have deeper ties into other services that they deliver to us.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: It should never be said that we are tied in to a vendor without having any kind of alternative options.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: And so we are committing to ensure that the Motorola

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: contracts, what they say they are going to deliver, they can in fact deliver, and they can deliver it on time,

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: in a timely way, with a budget that stays consistent and that is reliable, safe, and secure, and where everything stays up.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: So we are definitely looking into that.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: We should never be painting ourselves into a corner across the board where we are restricted to one vendor for life.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So could New York City operate and maintain this system tomorrow if Motorola suddenly stopped providing support?

chapters.summary: Council Member Felder asks whether the update was to software or hardware, noting both terms were used in testimony. Gelobter explains firewalls are physical hardware that run software/firmware, and this was a firmware update on the firewalls. Felder then asks about Verizon and T-Mobile's roles.
chapters.title: Felder clarifies whether update was software or hardware on firewalls

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Okay, a few more questions from me.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: So in the testimony, CTO, you testified that during the overnight hours of Monday, August 17th to Tuesday, August 18th, Motorola performed a software upgrade.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: that was deemed necessary and identified as routine to the firewalls in the routing environment located in PSAC 2.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Then it says, it is normal and intentional to apply updates to the hardware at PSAC.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: So my clarifying question is, was it a software update or a hardware update?

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Because both are stated.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Can you explain?

utterances.text: The difference.

utterances.text: This was an update to firmware on the firewalls.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: In your testimony, you also mentioned Verizon.

chapters.summary: Felder asks about Verizon's role and articles mentioning T-Mobile as a 911 network provider. Barbera clarifies Verizon is the E911 provider for NYC, and T-Mobile does not play a role in 911 call delivery within the city's infrastructure, though they provide 911 service to their customers. NextGen 911 is primarily a Motorola managed network.
chapters.title: Felder questions Verizon and T-Mobile roles in 911 system

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: But previously, I think Barbara.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Barbara testified about New York City Public Safety Network, and there are articles that mention T-Mobile as a network provider for 911.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: So who is the provider?

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Is it on an independent server?

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Like, what is the clarifying there?

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: The E911 provider for New York City is Verizon.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: That's the old system that we're working our way out.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: T-Mobile does not play a role in 911 call delivery within the city's infrastructure.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: So it is not a network provider, T-Mobile?

utterances.speaker: Speaker

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: And then next gen is fully Motorola.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: The primary core component to it is a Motorola managed network.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder

chapters.summary: Felder asks about Motorola's liability under the contract for service interruptions, indemnification provisions, and warranty disclaimers. Felder says they'll follow up with a letter.
chapters.title: Felder questions Motorola contract liability, indemnification, and warranties

utterances.text: Let me just find them.

utterances.text: Now, I appreciate the question.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: At this point, without having the full and complete root cause analysis, it would be premature to ascribe a particular liability.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: But we will explore not just the analysis of what happened, but also what any recourses may be.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: In terms of the contract, does the contract contain indemnification provisions applicable to an outage?

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: So I can't speak to the details of that, but what I will say is they are, in fact, required to provide an SLA, service level agreement.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: And so...

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: I can address some issues related to contract.

utterances.text: The contract includes terms that articulate contractor responsibilities and consequences.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: PA?

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: Deficiencies, I'll just keep going.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: Responsibilities, consequences, and deficiencies and failures.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: However, our investigation is ongoing.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: It would be irresponsible to comment on application of those contract terms at this time.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: I appreciate the question.

utterances.speaker: Speaker

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Does Motorola disclaim any warranties concerning the software or hardware used in the 911 system under contract?

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: If so, what warranties are disclaimed and what protections remain available to the city?

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: What I'd like to do is to, once we are through with the root cause analysis, we'll be able to answer a lot more of these questions in detail.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Felder asks about NYC Cyber Command's current responsibility for 911 cybersecurity, referencing 2022 testimony. Barbera explains there's joint management between OTI's public safety team and Cyber Command. Gelobter adds Cyber Command has a seat on the PSAC steering committee and lives within OTI, responsible for ensuring vendors meet strict cybersecurity requirements.
chapters.title: Felder questions Cyber Command's role in 911 cybersecurity

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: We're going to ask a few questions about the cyber command.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: And cybersecurity privacy and vendor security requirements.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: You previously testified in December 2022 that the New York City Cyber Command, I guess it was, I keep messing up your name, Barbara.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Barbara.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Barbara.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Barbara, I'm going to get it right.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: You previously testified in December 2022 that the New York City Cyber Command plays a central role in protecting the 911 system.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: What is the New York City Cyber Command's current responsibility for the cybersecurity of the 911 infrastructure?

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: Between the OTI public safety team and the cyber command team, there's a joint effort in unified management of all the cybersecurity infrastructure and services within 911.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: I would just add, so I think as I mentioned, there is a, PSAC is governed by a steering committee, and Cyber Command has a seat at that table.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: Thank you for that question.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: Yes, Cyber Command lives within OTI, and so it is our responsibility to make sure that any vendors, the software that they are creating for us,

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: as well as the hardware that they are putting into place, adheres to the strict requirements that we have around Cyber Command.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Has NYC3 or OTI conducted cybersecurity audits, penetration testing, vulnerability assessments, or other independent security reviews of the 911 systems?

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: If so, what was the most recent review, and were there any material vulnerabilities identified?

chapters.summary: Felder asks if OTI or Cyber Command has conducted cybersecurity audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments of 911 systems. Barbera confirms continuous monitoring 24/7, with penetration testing and vulnerability assessments conducted on an ongoing basis as part of strict implementation requirements.
chapters.title: Felder questions cybersecurity audits and penetration testing of 911

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: So there is a continuous monitoring activity between the public safety team and Cyber Command Security Operations Center that monitors the environment 24-7.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: There are specific requirements around system implementation that have to meet those very strict and stringent standards.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: That includes penetration testing and vulnerability.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: vulnerability assessments and those are repeated within the environment from a vulnerability detection standpoint on an ongoing basis.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Ongoing.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: As NextGen 911 begins accepting photographs, videos, text message, precise location information, and potentially other digital data, what policies will govern access, retention, sharing, and deletion of this information?

chapters.summary: Felder asks what policies will govern access, retention, sharing, and deletion of photographs, videos, and text messages that NextGen 911 will accept. Gelobter says they need to circle back, noting the Office of Privacy lives within OTI. Barbera clarifies those functions are not in phase one but in the next phase, requiring legal assessment of retention requirements.
chapters.title: Felder questions data privacy policies for NextGen 911 multimedia features

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: Thank you for the question.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: I think we will, unless you happen to know the answer off the top of your head, I think we need to circle back with you because I do think, again, we also have the

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: Office of Privacy lives in an OTI as well, and so ensuring that whatever we roll out with a NextGen 911 also adheres to best practices there.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: I don't have that answer in front of me, unless Rob does.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: With this phase of NextGen 911, those functions will not be implemented.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: That's in the next phase to come.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: That we would have to do a complete assessment to find out what the legal requirements are from a retention and evidence retention standpoint in order to, we'd work with the agencies to determine that.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

chapters.summary: Felder asks about the status of predictive analysis initiatives to stage first responders based on anticipated 911 demand. Barbera says this is part of NextGen 911 Phase 2, which hasn't started yet. Gelobter says they need to revisit previous plans and ensure whatever is built is correct, safe, and secure before adding features.
chapters.title: Felder questions predictive analytics and AI for first responder staging

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Shifting a little bit to predictive analytics and AI, in 2025, the city's Deputy Commissioner for Public Safety and Emergency Services discussed projects involving enhanced location

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: services and predictive analysis to help determine where first responders should be staged based on anticipated 911 demand.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: What is the current status of that initiative?

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: I believe you're referencing the NextGen 911 Phase 2 program.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: Due to the ongoing extension of the NextGen 911 call handling program, the Phase 2 program has

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: It started to a point where we have an executive strategy, and we are working now to prioritize items of how we will address them.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: The priority will be addressing any remaining items from the main phase of NextGen 911 with those additional features yet to come.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: So that has not started yet.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: And again, I would just say that until we have phase one buttoned up and we know when it actually can roll up in a way that is safe and secure, I think also at that point, we will take a closer look about what features and additions

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: do make sense, who they're serving, what problem they're solving, and again, making sure that they are safe and secure across the board.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: So I would just, I think we're going to have to take a finer look at.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: Whatever the previous plans were.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Okay, thank you for that answer.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: What does your office mean by predictive analysis in this context?

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: What information is being analyzed?

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: What predictions are being generated?

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: How are those predictions used operationally in terms of this initiative?

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: I would say that it's part of phase two, so I can't speak to a lot of the detail, and I think we need to revisit to make sure that whatever it is that we are building at that time is the correct stuff.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Okay, thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: We'll have more on that later on.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: I want to ask about AI specifically with Motorola.

chapters.summary: Felder asks if the city has implemented, tested, or contracted for any AI-enabled Motorola functionality. Gelobter says Motorola's AI capabilities are dependent on NextGen 911, which hasn't rolled out yet. AI is not part of phase one, and they will explore what makes sense to add after NextGen is live.
chapters.title: Felder questions Motorola AI-enabled capabilities in 911 system

utterances.text: Motorola has announced various AI-enabled public safety capabilities.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Has the city implemented, tested, or contracted for any AI-enabled Motorola functionality within the 911 system?

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: And again, it is not part of phase one.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: As we look at...

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: What being on NextGen 911, what features and assets it gives us, then we can explore and examine what it makes sense to add in and to augment the system with.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Thank you.

summary: Joint oversight hearing by four council committees examining the August 18, 2026 911 system outage that lasted approximately seven hours at the Bronx PSAC 2 center, affecting 1,696 calls including 742 911 calls, with 113 unique callers never connected to an operator.

CTO Lisa Gelobter testified that a Motorola Solutions firmware upgrade to PSAC 2 firewalls caused the outage; council members aggressively questioned monitoring failures, the hours-long delay in detecting 911 call impact, the absence of public notification via Notify NYC, and a previously undisclosed May 2026 text-to-911 outage.

Council members also pressed on NextGen 911 delays (now Q3 2027), 911 operator staffing and overtime, Motorola's contract liability and the city's dependence on the vendor, cybersecurity oversight, and the lack of a deadline for the root cause analysis; three members of the public testified including one advocating for an independent 911 system separate from NYPD.
